title: Bong Revilla's bail affirmed by Sandiganbayan
summary: The Sandiganbayan on Friday denied the Ombudsman"s appeal to reverse the court"s July 31 decision granting the bail petition filed by former Senator Ramon “Bong” Revilla, Jr., saying that the…

blocks.text: The Sandiganbayan on Friday denied the Ombudsman’s appeal to reverse the court’s July 31 decision granting the bail petition filed by former Senator Ramon “Bong” Revilla, Jr., saying that the prosecution’s evidence linking him to flood control kickback was not strong.
This stemmed from the P92.8-million malversation case filed against Revilla over a flood control project that was found to have no actual physical structure.

The Sandiganbayan said that Revilla’s role in supposedly ensuring that the said project would be funded under the General Appropriations Act is not the job of one person, given that the said proposed national budget is collectively approved by the House, the Senate, and the bicameral conference committee.

“The court maintained that the evidence adduced by the prosecution to prove overt acts of conspiracy on the part of accused Revilla was not strong. His (Revilla) participation in the legislative process was diluted and attenuated by the composition and structure of the Philippine Congress, as well as several institutional stages (or veto points) which a policy proposal must go through before its enactment as a law,” the Sandiganbayan said.

“Thus, it could not infer the overt act of facilitation from accused Revilla's Senate membership and Public Works Committee chairpersonship. Consequently, the chain of inference leading to the existence of conspiracy on the part of accused Revilla was broken,” it added.
Likewise, the anti-graft court cited that the case filed against Revilla would require malversation of public funds for a conviction, which the prosecution failed to prove during the bail hearings.

“The boxes of cash allegedly received by accused Revilla came from a pool of funds coming from private contractors. Even with testimonies narrating the general scheme within the Department of Public Works and Highways, the fundamental principle of in dubio pro reo (in applying and interpreting penal laws, to resolve all doubts in favor of the accused) would foreclose the characterization of these advance kickbacks as "public funds or property" in the context of malversation,” the Sandiganbayan said.

“Even if it were to be assumed that the prosecution had managed to adduce strong evidence of guilt that accused Revilla may have received cash from the private contractors, the same would only tend to prove the existence of bribery-an offense that is bailable as a matter of right regardless of whether the same is direct or indirect,” it added.
Further, the Sandiganbayan Third Division also denied the appeals for bail of Revilla’s co-accused.
These include former DPWH officials, namely: Brice Ericson Hernandez, Arjay Domasig, Jaypee Mendoza, Juanito Mendoza, Emelita Juat and Christina Pineda.
The anti-graft court said Revilla's co-accused did not dispute the prosecution’s allegations that the P92.8 million flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan was never built.

“As to accused Hernandez, Domasig, Jaypee and Juanito Mendoza, Juat, and Pineda, the Court ruled on the basis of the evidence of the prosecution considering that they had chosen to forgo their right to present rebuttal evidence. The discrepancy between the physical state of the subject project and the public records pertaining thereto, which the accused had signed in their official capacities as accountable officers, was strong evidence of their guilt of the crime of malversation,” the Sandiganbayan said.—LDF, GMA News
